# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial for Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)**
**Member:** Riley Jennings
**Member ID:** W995720068
**Reference Number:** POC-39DE00339B-16726
**Date of Denial Notice:** August 19, 2026
**Governing Policy:** UPMC Provider Manual Chapter G – Utilization Management (https://www.upmchealthplan.com/docs/providers/2025_ProviderManual_G.pdf)

Dear UPMC Health Plan Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a knee arthroscopy (CPT 29881), as stated in the notice referenced above. I am asking you to reconsider this decision.

## Why I Am Appealing

The denial notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already submitted address medical necessity in detail.

I want to note something important: the only plan citation I have been given in connection with this denial is language about prenatal visit scheduling (initial visit between 28 and 32 weeks, postpartum visit timing, and documentation of prenatal visit dates and risk factors). That language has nothing to do with knee arthroscopy or meniscus surgery, and it does not appear to be the criteria that were actually applied to my case. Because of this, I am not able to point to a specific plan criterion that my case supposedly fails to meet — I have not been given one that applies to this procedure. I am asking the plan to correct this and to identify the actual criteria used to review my request.

## The Medical Record

The following is what my medical record shows, as submitted in the prior authorization packet:

- **Symptom duration:** 9 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative care completed:** Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 10 weeks, from May 8, 2026 to July 17, 2026, with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; a corticosteroid injection on June 13, 2026 gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI of the knee on July 18, 2026, showing a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved; Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1.
- **Function:** I experience locking and giving way in the knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Other relevant history:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

I believe this record documents a specific structural diagnosis (a displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear causing mechanical locking), a completed and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection), and clear functional limitation. If the plan's own review criteria set out requirements in these areas, I believe the record above addresses them, and I am asking that it be reviewed against the actual criteria that apply to CPT 29881.

## Request for the Criteria Applied to My Case

I understand that UPMC Health Plan uses InterQual criteria in its utilization review process, and that this is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. I am nonetheless entitled to see the specific criteria used to deny my request. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must provide me, free of charge, with the specific rule or criterion relied upon in making this determination. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination** for CPT 29881, so that I can respond to it directly.

## What I Am Asking For

1. Please reconsider the denial of CPT 29881 in light of the clinical documentation summarized above.
2. Please provide, in writing, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and criteria text that were applied to my case, since the citation I have received so far does not pertain to this procedure.
3. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and let me know if any additional documentation is needed.

I understand my appeal must be received by February 15, 2027, which is within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, though I recognize the deadline stated on my denial letter is the controlling one. I am submitting this appeal by mail to the address printed on my denial notice. I understand I may also submit it through the member secure website, or reach the plan by phone at 1-888-876-2756 (group) or 1-866-353-3598 (individual), TTY 711.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Member signature]
Riley Jennings
Member ID: W995720068
[Date]
[Contact phone / email]

---

*This letter was prepared to help me communicate with my health plan. It is not medical or legal advice, and it does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
